title: Testing Data Integrity and Migrations
subtopics: Compatibility testing between application and database versions
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Testing Data Integrity and Migrations.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to constraint tests.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Testing Data Integrity and Migrations. Its primary job is to help you test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing testing data integrity and migrations teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Migration Release
content_blocks.alt_text: A migration release adds schema, deploys compatible code, backfills and verifies, then removes old structures later.
content_blocks.caption: Visual aid for Testing Data Integrity and Migrations. Use it alongside the subtopics and worked example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

items.title: Constraint tests
items.text: Relate this point to testing data integrity and migrations: define the expected behavior, one edge case, and a query or check that would provide evidence.

items.title: Transaction tests
items.text: Mark the transaction boundary explicitly and verify both the commit path and a rollback path in a disposable database.

items.title: Migration-upgrade tests
items.text: Prefer additive changes first, test against populated sample data, and preserve compatibility while old and new code overlap.

items.title: Rollback and recovery tests
items.text: Mark the transaction boundary explicitly and verify both the commit path and a rollback path in a disposable database.

items.title: Compatibility testing between application and database versions
items.text: Prefer additive changes first, test against populated sample data, and preserve compatibility while old and new code overlap.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Testing Data Integrity and Migrations
content_blocks.code: ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN marketing_opt_in boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
content_blocks.expected_output: Existing rows receive the default according to PostgreSQL semantics; verify lock and rewrite characteristics for the actual version and table.
content_blocks.safety_note: Schema changes can lock or rewrite data; rehearsal and rollback planning are required.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run only in a local migration test against representative populated data.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For a read-only SELECT or inspection command, no reset is needed. For DDL/DML, use a disposable database; capture the starting state, run the example, inspect the result, and ROLLBACK or drop the lab objects as appropriate. Do not use production data or credentials.
content_blocks.limitations: CodeLeaf currently previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute PostgreSQL queries, shell commands or Python in the lesson page. Treat the sample as inspectable code unless you run it yourself in an approved isolated environment. Python examples require a separate isolated runner.
content_blocks.schema_assumptions: Run only in a local migration test against representative populated data.

content_blocks.title: Practical checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Safety checkpoint: use least-privilege credentials, synthetic data, and a separate test database; verify results before applying a change to a real workload.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Testing Data Integrity and Migrations”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “Constraint tests”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “Constraint tests”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Testing Data Integrity and Migrations, with an explanation of “Constraint tests”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Testing Data Integrity and Migrations fits into the broader goal to test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review.
Use the curriculum subtopics as a completeness checklist: Constraint tests, Transaction tests, Migration-upgrade tests.
State the schema/version assumptions and verify one normal case plus an edge case before trusting the result.
